t: Amsterdam grew from a settlement at a dam on the Amstel, first named in 1275, into a trading town of the County of Holland that lived from beer, herring, and grain and timber from the Baltic.

In the 17th century, after the Dutch Revolt and the fall of Antwerp, it became the leading port and financial centre of the western world, with the Dutch East India Company, a bank and a stock exchange, and its canals were built around the old town.

The city declined in the 18th and early 19th centuries, revived with the North Sea Canal and industry, and in the Second World War lost most of its Jewish population, who had made up about a tenth of its people.
dyk: In 1452 a fire destroyed three quarters of Amsterdam, and Emperor Charles decreed that new houses were to be built of stone; the Wooden House in the Begijnhof is one of the few wooden buildings left from this period.
ev: The All Saints' Flood turns the IJ into a wide estuary and gives the Amstel an open connection to the Zuiderzee
Count Floris V grants the residents of Amestelledamme an exemption from tolls
Amsterdam changes sides in the Alteratie and joins the revolt against Spain
The Dutch East India Company is founded, with its Amsterdam office trading in its own shares
The plague kills more than a tenth of the population, with 24,148 buried in that year
The Netherlands is conquered by France and the old Republic becomes the Batavian Republic
The North Sea Canal opens and gives the port a direct route to the sea
Nazi Germany invades the Netherlands and occupies Amsterdam until 1945

f.founded: The settlement grew at the mouth of the Amstel after the flood of 1170, and a dam there is estimated to date from between 1264 and 1275. It is first named in a document of 27 October 1275, which gave its residents an exemption from tolls.
f.where: At the mouth of the Amstel river, where it meets the IJ, in the province of North Holland in the western Netherlands, about 2 metres below sea level.
f.known: The dam in the Amstel and the toll privilege of 1275; herring and the Baltic grain trade; the Dutch Golden Age of the 17th century; the Dutch East India Company and its stock exchange; the canal ring; religious refuge for Jews, Huguenots and others; Rembrandt; the occupation of 1940 to 1945 and the deportation of its Jews
f.today: Amsterdam is the capital and largest city of the Netherlands, though the government and parliament sit in The Hague.
